newsitem.title: UK: UK gilt futures end higher, aided by strong stg.
newsitem.headline: UK gilt futures end higher, aided by strong stg.

text.p: 1623 GMT - UK gilt futures ended higher, buoyed by the strength of sterling and steady demand from institutions in Britain and abroad. Wednesday's jobs and earnings data are expected to be favourable, Bank of England Inflation Report is awaited with interest. * March contract ends up 13/32 at 113-10
"Sterling continues to storm upwards and that's obviously attracting overseas interest as well," he added.
The pound soared over three pfennigs to a new 52-month peak of 2.7460 against the deutschemark and analysts expect it to advance further.
The gilt-Bund spread at 10 years narrowed to 166 basis points from 168 at the previous close.
Wednesday's UK unemployment, average earnings and unit wage costs data are expected to be generally positive for gilts.
The Bank of England's quarterly Inflation Report at 1130 GMT tomorrow is also keenly awaited.
Analysts expect the central bank to renew its warnings about inflation on a two-year timescale and to press for a tightening in monetary policy.
Rayner said any sign that the Bank has softened its previous argument that the strength of sterling is unlikely to have a major deflationary impact would be taken well by the market.
March short sterling ended one basis point higher at 93.71, implying official interest rates of around 6.30 percent at the end of the first quarter compared wiht 6.0 percent now.
